sentences.text: The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - original claimant, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 18.11.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Vadodara, in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.999 of 2015, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.9,01,367/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1.

The claim petition arises out of an accident that occurred on 23/07/2015 at about 10.15 a.m in Jambusar ST bus depot, within the jurisdiction of Jambusar police station NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3554/2021 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined of Bharuch District.

On the day of incident, the claimant was waiting for the ST bus at the Jambusar ST Depot for going to Bharuch and at that time the Bansidhar Parsottambhai Bhatt vs Iqbal Ahmed Shelat on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189848344/
1 opponent No.1 came driving ST bus bearing registration No.GJ-18-Y-6260 and while boarding on the ST bus, the driver of the ST bus suddenly start the bus, resultant, he fell down from the bus and the wheel of the bus run over his left leg and hand and thereby the accident had taken place in which he sustained severe crush injuries.

sentences.text:
Thus, the accident had taken place because of rash and negligent driving on the part of the ST bus driver involved in the accident and against the driver of the ST Bus,
offences has been registered under CR No.35/2015. 2.2 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal has been preferred before this Court for enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard learned advocate Mr. Hiren M. Modi for the appellant and learned advocate Mr. Tanmay B. Karia for the respondent No.2 - GSRTC.
Though served, none appears for the respondent No.1.

4. Learned advocate Mr. Hiren M. Modi appearing for the appellant-claimant submitted that the tribunal has awarded NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3554/2021 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined lesser amount to the tune of Rs.9,01,367/-
with 9% interest per annum and tribunal has not properly considered the future loss of income.

He has further submitted that though the disability is considered properly of 50% and the multiplier 5 is considered is found just and proper but under the head of pain, shock and suffering, considering the hospitalization of the claimant and looking to the fractures and crush injuries and multiple surgeries, the amount towards pain, shock and suffering should be at least more than Rs.80,000/-, which is required to be awarded, whereas, only Rs.50,000/- came to be awarded by the tribunal and therefore, enhancement is prayed for under the head of pain, shock and suffering.
He has further submitted that under the head of special diet, attendant charges and transportation, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.20,000/-, which ought to have been awarded at least Rs.40,000/-.

4.1 Learned advocate Mr. Modi has further submitted that considering the injuries received by the claimant, the amount towards the loss of amenities is required to be awarded appropriately or at least Rs.50,000/- could be awarded under the head of loss of amenities.
He has submitted that amount of Rs.6,61,367/- under the head of medical expenses came to be awarded, which are as per the bill and therefore, there cannot be any enhancement.

He has submitted that at least NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3554/2021 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined further enhancement to the tune of Rs.2 to 2.5 lakhs can be awarded considering the above-mentioned difference in the awarded amount by the tribunal and therefore, he prays to allow the present appeal by awarding further enhancement in the amount awarded by the tribunal.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Tanmay B. Karia appearing for the respondent No.2- Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation has submitted that the judgment and Bansidhar Parsottambhai Bhatt vs Iqbal Ahmed Shelat on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189848344/
2 award passed by the tribunal is just and proper and the tribunal has awarded amount to the tune of Rs.9,01,367/- for the injury case, which is more than sufficient.

sentences.text: He has submitted that though there is some minor scope for enhancement but under the heads of pain, shock and suffering as well as loss of amenities, no further enhancement can be granted.

Therefore, he has submitted that the tribunal has considered the entire evidence and discussed in detail with regard to the oral as well as documentary evidence and thereafter, has come to the conclusion and awarded the amount.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

7. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3554/2021 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
7.1 It transpires from the record that the tribunal has awarded Rs.1,50,000/- towards future loss of income by considering income of Rs.5,000/- per month.

It transpires from the record that the claimant was earning and was serving as a teacher and was also possessing 8 bighas of agricultural land in his own name and 60 bighas land in joint names and he was earning more than Rs.4 lakhs per annum from the agricultural produce.
The tribunal has not considered all these aspects in proper context.

Therefore, considering the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram and Ors reported NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3554/2021 ORDER DATED:
14/06/2024 undefined in (2018) 18 SCC 130 as well as New India Assurance Company Limited Vs.
Somwati and Ors. reported in (2020) 9 SCC 644, the amount which is awarded by the tribunal is required to be reconsidered and to be awarded accordingly.

Though the claimant has tried to narrate that he is owning the agricultural land in his name and he was serving as a teacher but no documentary evidence is available on record to prove his case.

Therefore, in that case, the tribunal ought to have considered the aspect that the minimum wages is required to be awarded considering the qualification of the claimant and considering the nature of job he could have done.

The minimum wages which is prevalent in the year 2015, when the accident has occurred on 23.07.2015;
at least income should be considered Rs.7,239/- per month instead of Rs.5,000/- per month, which is taken by the tribunal.

Therefore, considering that income and multiplying it by 12, it comes to Bansidhar Parsottambhai Bhatt vs Iqbal Ahmed Shelat on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189848344/

which is multiplied by 5 multiplier, it comes to Rs.2,17,170/-, therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3554/2021 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined under the head of future loss of income,
amount ought to have been awarded Rs.2,17,170/-.

sentences.text: Tribunal has committed error in awarding Rs.1,50,000/- and thereby, as per discussed above, Rs.2,17,170/- is awarded by this Court under the head of future loss of income.

The actual loss of income should be considered for six months looking to the nature of injury, which the tribunal has considered only for four months, therefore,
considering the amount, Rs.7,239/- is required to be considered for loss of one month and for six months, actual loss of income comes to the tune of Rs.43,434/-, and therefore, the amount which is awarded by the tribunal under the head of actual loss of income i.e. Rs.20,000/- is required to be enhanced to the tune of Rs.43,434/-.

7.3 Under the head of pain, shock and suffering, the tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/-, considering the discussion about the injuries received by the claimant, it is required to be noted from the discharge summary issued by the hospital which is produced at Exhs.30 and 31, it appears that the claimant had sustained serious crush injury with open communicated fracture humerus fracture left tibia fibula, metatarsal 2, 5 th head fracture and shaft of 4 th metatarsal, proximal phalanx of 3 and 5 th toes, cuneiform bone and was treated for crush injury of left forearm and multiple surgeries were done including wound debridement and fixation of left NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3554/2021 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined humerus,
flap coverage and skin grafting.

Therefore, considering the nature of injury and treatment period, I am of the opinion that at least Rs.70,000/- under the head of pain, shock and suffering is required to be awarded, whereas, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.50,000/-, therefore, further amount is awarded to the tune of Rs.70,000/- under the head of pain, shock and suffering.
Considering the amount awarded under the of transportation, attendant charges and special diet, tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-.

Considering the nature of injury and hospitalization, at least Rs.30,000/- is required to be awarded and therefore, the amount is enhanced to Rs.30,000/- under the head of transportation, attendant charges and special diet.
7.4 Tribunal has failed to award amount under the head of loss of amenities.

Now, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has said in certain cases where such injuries are received by the claimant; tribunal ought to grant some amount towards the loss of amenities and therefore, looking to the injuries received by the claimant and the period of hospitalization as well as considering his future life, at least Rs.30,000/- is required to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities, accordingly,
Rs.30,000/- is hereby awarded.

Under the head of medical expenses, tribunal awarded Rs.6,61,367/-, which is discussed in para 21 of the impugned order, such amount is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3554/2021 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined awarded as per the endorsement given by both the advocates, therefore, that amount is not required to be disturbed and Rs.6,61,367/- is required to be awarded under the head of medical expenses.

7.5 Thus, the appellant - claimant is entitled to get the following final amount as compensation:

7.6

Tribunal has already awarded Rs.9,01,367/-, therefore,
deducting that amount, further enhancement of Rs.1,50,604/- is required to be awarded by allowing the present appeal.

The respondent No.2-S.T. Corporation shall deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.1,50,604/- with 9%
interest per annum from the date of claim petition till the actual realization before the concerned tribunal within a period of 4 weeks from today.

7.8 On deposition of such amount, the Tribunal shall immediately disburse the entire awarded amount (including the enhanced amount) lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimant, by account payee cheque or by transferring the entire awarded amount in the bank account of the claimant, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
8. The present appeal is allowed to the aforesaid extent by enhancing the awarded amount to the tune of Rs.1,50,604/-, in addition to the amount awarded by the concerned tribunal.
9. Record and proceedings, if any, lying before this Court shall be sent forthwith to the concerned tribunal.
